newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister sees sell-off deal with hard-left.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister sees sell-off deal with hard-left.

text.p: Italian Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani said in an interview published on Monday that he believed the government and the hard-left Communist Refoundation could reach agreement on privatisations.

Bersani, in an interview in the Corriere della Sera daily, said he had been taking part in discussions between the centre-left coalition of Prime Minister Romano Prodi and the Refoundation. "There is room for agreement," he said.

The Communist Refoundation is not in the coalition, but holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament. It is opposed to the sell-off of certain state companies, especially the utilities.
"We are working towards guaranteeing that markets are opened and to avoid the simple passage of public monopolies to private monopolies," Bersani said.
The government hopes to sell state controlled telecom giant Stet, this autumn and a thrid tranche of energy group Eni. Plans are also afoot to sell-off electricity utility Enel.

It announced on Friday that it would maintain a so-called 'golden share' in Stet following the sell-off, enabling it to influence policy despite losing its majority stake. Refoundation had demanded that the state retain a say in the running of Stet.
